Done. The export passed on the first execution and all artifacts are under `out/T3/`.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T3/solution.py` using plain torch and safetensors. It casts the 48 projection matrices to bfloat16 with anchored regexes, drops the 12 causal-mask buffers, and keeps the other 100 tensors float32 and bit-identical.
- The four required checks run before any file is written, plus extra guards. These cover input tensor count, cast and drop counts, the float32 count, and a bit-exact comparison of every uncast tensor against the source.
- Sharding is greedy in natural key order with a 64 MiB budget. The oversized embedding is placed alone in its own shard.
- After writing, the script reloads every shard and verifies each key against the index plus dtype, shape and values.

**Result of the single run**

| shard | tensors | tensor bytes |
|---|---|---|
| model-00001-of-00005 | 3 | 3,151,872 |
| model-00002-of-00005 | 1 (wte.weight) | 154,389,504 |
| model-00003-of-00005 | 59 | 66,259,968 |
| model-00004-of-00005 | 58 | 66,256,896 |
| model-00005-of-00005 | 27 | 37,831,680 |

Total 148 tensors, 48 bfloat16, 100 float32, with an index file mapping every name to its shard.

**Tool choice**

I did not use `transformers.save_pretrained` or mergekit because both apply one dtype globally, and reloading through the model class would re-add the mask buffers. A short script gave exact control over the key set and per-tensor dtypes.

`out/T3/REPORT.md` contains the self-report with the fields from the record template. It notes one open assumption: the grader checks sharding rules rather than an exact shard assignment, since the task does not specify the reference packing order.
